correctness.rationale: Exact unit-circumradius simplex vertex normalization and Haar normal representation yield the standardized Gaussian exceedance count (4). Crossing simplex faces gives the finite combinatorial formula (3). A moving empirical-threshold expansion gives the iid influence function with both first and second Gaussian Hermite corrections; their orthogonality yields the exact positive variance. Multivariate fixed-rank polynomial delta methods yield (1) at fixed nonzero offset and (2) for offset lambda/sqrt(m). All nonstandard analytical steps are explicitly shown; the 3551 diagnostic checks independently reproduce finite combinatorics and geometry, numerical variance and both limiting normalizations. No simulation is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Closest full published face-vector and chi-square results cover only centroidal hyperplanes. Off-center unit normals require studentized Gaussian residuals, with a distinct analytic influence variance at fixed nonzero displacement and a noncentral chi-square joint face-vector law at physical inverse-dimension displacement. Full accessible central/noncentral primary volume papers do not state these probabilistic face-count laws. Historical originality is best-knowledge, not independently certified.
residual_risks: A historical result in the statistics literature on studentized Gaussian empirical distributions, combined with a combinatorial section formula, might imply some limiting laws even if not titled geometrically.
Some older or unindexed mathematical papers and full article proofs may cover special cases; bibliographic searching is not a uniqueness proof.
The related moving-axis-point Haar hyperplane model has a different joint offset-normal sampling measure and does not imply the deterministic-signed-offset theorem.
This assessment is same-author mathematical review and has not undergone independent validation.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated change from Haar centroidal to Haar affine simplex sections produces a sharp geometric scale crossover: fixed standardized nonzero offsets give rank-one Gaussian face vectors, whereas physical displacements of order 1/m yield rank-one noncentral chi-square deficits. The variance formula exhibits the sample-centering and length-normalization correction that is absent from naive binomial heuristics. The precise distinction extends previous random section results to a new geometric sampling regime with interpretable equality and scaling boundaries.
